title: extcap: handle control in pipe in extcap, not qt
description:
Fulfill half of a long-standing TODO by moving the control in pipe
handling to extcap, instead of Qt. This makes the extcap control in
    pipe handling much more similar to the dumpcap sync pipe in handing
    (though on Windows extcap uses OVERLAPPED I/O where dumpcap doesn't,
    and extcap uses named pipes that are opened by name by the extcaps
    instead of inheriting file descriptors/HANDLEs that are already open.)
    
The motivation for doing this is so that the control pipe can be used
    for _other_ sync pipe command types besides SP_TOOLBAR_CTRL, especially
    SP_LOG_MSG and SP_ERROR_MSG and SP_WARNING_MSG, so that those sorts of
    messages can be sent with structure and handled appropriately, instead
    of already formatted strings sent to stderr. The current structure means
    that warnings can't be displayed as they come in, only at the end of
    the capture, the total amount of warnings is limited, etc. That makes it
    hard to display gracefully a message like "the host key was added to
    known_hosts" at the start of a capture.
    
We can't just assume that everything coming in on stderr is formatted
    according to the sync pipe protocol, for the same reasons as #12222 on dumpcap.
    Stdout and stdin could possibly be used, if we could guarantee that the
    extcaps when spawned as children didn't write anything to stdout that wasn't
    formatted according to the sync pipe protocol.

We want to handle the control pipe in extcap instead of the Qt UI
    Interface Toolbar so that it will work when extcaps are used by tshark
    or other non Qt UIs.
    
Doing the same thing for the control out pipe could address #17131
